events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to Grand Haven.** I'd expect a below-average pier night at best, about a 1 out of 4, with a few salmon possible.
- **Fish spoons, especially glow spoons, in low light** (early morning or evening). Glow plugs are the other option the reports mention.
- **St. Joseph, South Haven and Muskegon are my lower picks.** I'd expect a 0-1 at St. Joseph, and I have no recent pier salmon reports for South Haven or Muskegon to rate.

## Why

- **Grand Haven has the most consistent pier catches:** the last two Grand Haven pier reports both rated 1, with a few salmon on spoons (Grand Haven, 2023-08-30; 2023-08-23).
- **St. Joseph's latest pier report was slow:** pier anglers "who targeted trout and salmon had slow fishing" (St. Joseph, 2023-08-30).
- **Warming water argues against a pier bite right now:** the Grand Haven and Muskegon buoy rose 12 F over the last week, which is the opposite of the sharp drop that signals upwelling. I'd expect fewer salmon pushed to the piers this week.

## Evidence

**Recent reports (latest is 2023-08-30, 6 days old)**
- Grand Haven, 2023-08-30, pier: "Pier anglers caught a few salmon while casting spoons in low light conditions." Quality 1 (below average). Spoons.
- Grand Haven, 2023-08-23, pier: "A few salmon were caught off the piers while casting glow spoons." Quality 1. Glow spoons.
- Grand Haven, 2023-08-16, pier: "Pier anglers who were casting spoons found the freshwater drum and salmon bite to be slow." Quality 0. Glow spoons and plugs worked.
- St. Joseph, 2023-08-30, pier: "Pier anglers who targeted trout and salmon had slow fishing." Quality 0.
- St. Joseph, 2023-08-09, pier: a few coho on nightcrawlers, quality 1, "a little on the slow side."
- South Haven and Muskegon: no pier salmon observations in the last six weeks. Their reports covered boats only.
- Boats were doing better at Grand Haven (2023-08-30, quality 3, 40–80 ft, glow or chrome J-plugs), but that's not the pier plan you asked about.

**Past seasons (history, similar water temperature near 65 F in early Sept.)**
- Grand Haven pier in a similar week (2023-08-23 and 2023-08-16) was 0-1: a few fish on glow spoons, otherwise slow.
- St. Joseph, 2022-08-17 (buoy 65 F, after an upwelling drop): "There were a few Chinook caught but it was mostly all steelhead," with a few salmon on spoons and spinners (quality 1).
- I'd expect the pier to stay slow to fair through the next week or so, consistent with these past weeks.

**Conditions now**
- Buoy surface water over the week before today: Grand Haven and Muskegon 63 F (+12 F over the week); St. Joseph 71 F (+4 F); South Haven 68 F (+5 F). These are the most recent measured values I have.
- No modeled pierhead temperature or wind forecast came back, so I can't confirm whether an upwelling is building near the piers.

## Caveats

- The newest reports are from 2023-08-30, six days old, and the season changes quickly in early fall. Treat these ratings as a guide.
- The temperatures are measured buoy values from the week before today, not live readings. The pierhead model and wind forecast weren't available, so I couldn't check for a fresh upwelling.
- Pier data is thin: South Haven and Muskegon have no recent pier salmon reports, so their ratings are guesses from boat reports and history.
- The ratings are my expectations based on these reports, not forecasts from the DNR.

## Sources

- Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph bulletin, 2023-08-23: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/36c669b
- Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph bulletin, 2023-08-16: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/36b27d5
- St. Joseph bulletin, 2022-08-17 (history): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3288194
